column4: Sun and moon are said to move by a calculation; this directly sharpens the section's image of their measured order.
The verse names night, day, sun, and moon together, with each swimming in an orbit; it is a compact parallel to the section's ordered celestial scene.
The oath by dawn uses the source-section's root ف ج ر for daybreak, the light that breaks into the night in the section's dictionary image.
The verse says garments protect from heat and violence (“تَقِيكُمُ”); this is a Quranic concrete use of the source-section root و ق ي for protective covering.
The preceding oath turns to retreating stars before the departing night and breathing dawn of 81:17–18; it extends that passage's transition from covered sky to morning.
The next description says these stars move and disappear, continuing 81:15's retreating-star scene before the night and dawn of 81:17–18.
At the world's ending the sun is folded up, a direct reversal of the section's sun as a source whose light spreads.
The resurrection scene begins with sight being dazzled; it marks a boundary to the section's stable, visible celestial order.
The moon is eclipsed, reversing its ordered following and fullness in the section's sky image.
The sun and moon are brought together, a direct reversal of their ordered separation in 36:40 and the section's successive sky roles.
On the day hidden things are exposed (“السَّرَائِرُ”), the section's movement from visible light to self-concealment is reversed into disclosure.
The cloud is made a shade over the people; it gives a Quranic cloud-cover scene that parallels the source section's secondary cloud image over the sun.
God protects the righteous from that day's evil and gives them radiance and joy; this connects the source-section's protective sense of و ق ي with its light imagery.
The person who gives and is mindful supplies a concrete moral counterpart to the section's taqwa as the soul's protective orientation.
The one who gives and is mindful is facilitated toward ease; this parallels the section's success for the soul cultivated in taqwa.
The opposite person withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, giving a specific moral contrast to the section's fujur and self-burying.
The withholding person's path is facilitated toward hardship; this makes explicit the failure-side outcome parallel to the section's contrast between purification and concealment.
The most mindful is kept away from the Fire; this gives a concrete protective outcome to the section's account of taqwa.
The verse uses ḍuḥā as a portion of the day that seems brief at the resurrection; it extends the section's measured morning interval into a perspective on time's passing.
Night is for rest and day is made “مُبْصِرًا”; this repeats the section's specific cover-and-seeing pair.
